Forest Roads: Riding Through Britain's Woodlands

Forest riding offers a completely different atmosphere from open moorland and coastal roads. Light filters through canopy, the air is cool and fragrant, and the road winds between ancient trees. Britain has more woodland than you might expect, and some of the finest roads in the country pass through it.

Scotland's Forest Roads

  • Rothiemurchus Forest, Cairngorms: The road through Rothiemurchus from Aviemore to Loch Morlich passes through ancient Caledonian pine forest — the remnant of the vast forest that once covered Scotland. Red squirrels, crossbills, and capercaillie inhabit these woods.
  • Galloway Forest Park: The A712 Queen's Way through Galloway Forest is one of Scotland's finest forest roads. It passes through the UK's first Dark Sky Park, alongside lochs and through towering Sitka spruce.
  • Glen Affric: Often called the most beautiful glen in Scotland. The single-track road through Glen Affric penetrates ancient pine and birch woodland of extraordinary beauty.
  • Argyll Forest Park: The A83 through the Rest and Be Thankful passes through dense forest with dramatic mountain views above the treeline.

England's Forest Roads

  • New Forest, Hampshire: Britain's newest national park is a patchwork of ancient woodland, heath, and open forest. The B-roads winding through ancient oaks and beeches are atmospheric, especially in autumn when the colours are stunning.
  • Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire: On the Welsh border, this ancient royal forest contains miles of riding roads through dense mixed woodland. The Speech House road through the heart of the forest is particularly fine.
  • Kielder Forest, Northumberland: England's largest forest. The road from Bellingham to Kielder village passes through vast plantations beside Kielder Water. Remote and atmospheric.
  • Dalby Forest, North York Moors: A toll road through the forest (£10 for motorcycles) offers a unique canopy ride through this managed forest.

Wales's Forest Roads

  • Coed y Brenin, Snowdonia: The forest roads around this Forestry Commission site near Dolgellau are surrounded by mature woodland with rivers and waterfalls.
  • Brechfa Forest, Carmarthenshire: Remote forest with narrow roads winding through dense woodland. Peaceful and atmospheric.
Forest roads demand specific attention. The road surface is often damp under canopy even when surrounding roads are dry. Leaf litter in autumn can be treacherous. And wildlife — deer especially — can appear suddenly from the treeline. Moderate your speed and enjoy the atmosphere.

Seasonal Forest Riding

  • Spring: Bluebells carpet the woodland floor in May. The effect through ancient deciduous woodland is magical.
  • Summer: Full canopy provides welcome shade on hot days. The temperature under trees can be 5°C cooler than open roads.
  • Autumn: Peak forest riding season. Reds, golds, and oranges transform deciduous woodland into a colour spectacle.
  • Winter: Bare branches reveal the architecture of the trees. Frost-covered forests in morning light are hauntingly beautiful.

Forest roads add variety and atmosphere to any motorcycle tour. They're a reminder that Britain, despite its reputation for open moorland, is still a land of ancient trees and deep woodland.
keyTakeaways: Forest roads offer cool, fragrant, canopy-shaded riding quite different from moorland and coast.
Rothiemurchus in the Cairngorms and Glen Affric are ancient Caledonian pine at its finest.
England's New Forest, Forest of Dean, and Kielder deliver miles of atmospheric woodland riding.
Autumn is peak forest season for colour, while spring brings bluebells and summer brings welcome shade.
Damp surfaces under canopy, autumn leaf litter, and sudden deer all demand a moderated pace.

faq.q: Why do forest roads need extra care?
faq.a: The canopy keeps the surface damp long after surrounding roads have dried, so grip is often lower than you expect. In autumn, fallen leaves form a slippery layer that hides the surface and reduces traction, especially on bends. Deer and other wildlife can step from the treeline without warning, so moderate your speed, read the road ahead, and enjoy the atmosphere rather than chasing pace.

faq.q: When is the best season for forest riding?
faq.a: Autumn is the highlight, when deciduous woodland turns to reds, golds, and oranges, making rides through the New Forest and Forest of Dean spectacular. Spring brings carpets of bluebells in May, summer offers cool shade several degrees below open-road temperatures, and even winter has appeal when bare branches and frost transform the woods. Each season gives forest roads a distinct character.

faq.q: Are these forest roads open to motorcycles?
faq.a: The public roads through these forests, such as the A712 Queen's Way and the New Forest B-roads, are ordinary rights of way open to bikes. A few, like Dalby Forest in the North York Moors, are toll roads with a charge for motorcycles. Off-road forestry tracks are generally not open to road bikes, so stick to the surfaced public roads.

faq.q: Which forest road is best for combining with stargazing?
faq.a: Galloway Forest Park is ideal. The A712 Queen's Way is a fine forest road by day, and the park is Britain's first Dark Sky Park with designated star-gazing sites for a clear night after riding. Kielder Forest in Northumberland pairs vast, remote woodland roads with Europe's largest area of Dark Sky Park, making it another superb ride-and-stargaze combination.
